clue.text: Republican greeting flipping angry prisoner — one has a thick skin

parts.note: hi is a casual greeting

indicators.note: flipping turns the words for angry and prisoner over so they read from the back

parts.note: sore can mean angry or aggrieved
con is short for convict, a prisoner

explanation.surface: A Republican's hello turns sour as an angry inmate bristles, while someone thick-skinned shrugs it off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' reverses SORECON to NOCEROS, which follows R and HI.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhinoceros is famous for its tough, armour-like hide.

clue.text: Strong old labourer finally lifted chest

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifted means these letters are read upwards, so backwards
finally picks only the closing letter of the word labourer

parts.note: bust means chest

explanation.surface: A sturdy old workman finally hoists a heavy chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted' reverses OR to RO in this down answer; BUST follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Robust is a synonym of strong, sturdy and vigorous.

clue.text: Something on a mountain, say, that is restricting cold? A hat

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the letters for that is close around cold

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
a cap is a hat

explanation.surface: On a cold mountain peak, a hat is just the thing to keep the chill off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restricting' puts C inside IE to make ICE.
explanation.definitionFit: An icecap is a permanent covering of ice, found for instance on a high summit, so it is one example of what sits on a mountain.

clue.text: Bit of lore from old salt we've intoxicated touring island

indicators.note: touring means going around, so the shuffled letters surround the island letter
intoxicated means drunk, so these words stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A tipsy old sailor spins yarns as he and his shipmates tour an island.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters of OLD SALT WEVE go around I.
explanation.definitionFit: An old wives' tale is a piece of traditional folk belief, often superstition, passed on by word of mouth.

clue.text: Some giant eruption up here?

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters run upwards, so backwards
some means only a portion of these words supplies the letters

explanation.surface: A volcano asks whether a huge eruption might happen right here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes ANTE from giANT Eruption; 'up' reverses it. The whole clue also points to the volcano.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna in Sicily is Europe's most active volcano, famous for big eruptions.

clue.text: Far out, where Humpty fell?

definitions.meaning: far out is slang for eccentric or unconventional
Humpty Dumpty sat on a wall and had a great fall, literally coming off it

explanation.definitionFit: Off-the-wall means bizarre or unconventional; literally, it is the place Humpty Dumpty tumbled from in the nursery rhyme.

clue.text: Vile, horrible

indicators.note: horrible suggests something mangled, so the letters of the preceding word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Two near-synonyms side by side describe something truly nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horrible' rearranges VILE; the whole clue doubles as the meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Evil means wicked and morally bad, close in sense to vile and horrible.

clue.text: Vet covers places with variable rate

indicators.note: covers means the word vet wraps around the word for places

parts.note: loci is the plural of locus, a place
y is a typical algebraic variable

explanation.surface: A vet charges different amounts at different clinics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vet' looks like the animal doctor or a verb meaning check, but here it is just three letters for 'covers' to wrap around.
explanation.definitionFit: Velocity is speed in a direction, a rate of motion.

clue.text: Identified boy embracing beautiful girl

indicators.note: embracing means holding, so the boy's word goes round the girl's

parts.note: lad means boy
a belle is a beautiful woman or girl

explanation.surface: A boy is spotted with his arms around a pretty girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embracing' signals the boy's word holding the girl's inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To be labelled is to be tagged or named, so identified.

clue.text: Bake friend rolls — cut them with this

definitions.text: Bake friend rolls — cut them with this

indicators.note: rolls means turns over, so the letters of the two words tumble into a new order

explanation.surface: Baking rolls for a friend, then slicing them with the right tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rolls' anagrams BAKE FRIEND; as a noun it is also the bread being cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A bread knife, with its serrated blade, is the tool for slicing loaves and rolls.

clue.text: This might be used for putting young animal outside pound

definitions.text: This might be used for putting

indicators.note: outside means the young animal's word sits around the pound letter

parts.note: a cub is a young animal such as a fox or bear
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Something for putting a young animal outside the dog pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' wraps CUB around L. 'putting' is golf, not placing.
explanation.definitionFit: A golf club, specifically the putter, strikes the ball on the green.

clue.text: Working a lot, Parisian's ambitious

indicators.note: working means being worked over, so these letters are reshaped

parts.note: the letters of a lot and Parisian are shuffled; the 's stands for is, linking to the definition

explanation.surface: Someone from Paris is putting in long hours, keen to get ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working' rearranges A LOT PARISIAN; the 's means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspirational describes someone with high hopes of success.

clue.text: Government virtually in charge, still

indicators.note: virtually means almost, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: the state is the government of a country

explanation.surface: A government that is nearly in charge is simply standing still.
explanation.walkthrough: 'virtually' trims STATE to STAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Static means motionless, unmoving.

clue.text: Material they use regularly captured in picture by a student

indicators.note: captured in means held inside the word for picture

parts.note: pic is short for picture

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter from the words they use

parts.note: L is the learner, a student driver

explanation.surface: The fabric they keep using appears in a picture taken by a student.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of 'they use'; 'captured in' holds them inside the picture word.
explanation.definitionFit: Physical and material both mean relating to tangible matter rather than the mind.

clue.text: Mark's trendy way of speaking including American

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, joining the definition mark to the wordplay

parts.note: in means fashionable

indicators.note: including means the word for way of speaking takes the American letter inside it

parts.note: diction is a manner of speaking

explanation.surface: Mark adopts a fashionable accent that includes some American twang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'including' puts A inside DICTION.
explanation.definitionFit: An indication is a sign or mark showing something.

clue.text: One might blow this small bit of money while going round street

parts.note: a penny is a small coin

indicators.note: going round means the word while encircles the street abbreviation

explanation.surface: Someone might squander a small sum while wandering the streets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blow' looks like squandering money, but it means playing an instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A penny whistle is a simple tin flute that you play by blowing.

clue.text: This is radioactive waste not beginning to eat a metal

indicators.note: to eat means the remaining letters take the following ones inside them
not beginning means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: taken as written
tin is a metal

explanation.surface: Radioactive waste eats away at a piece of metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not beginning' trims WASTE to ASTE; 'to eat' puts ATIN inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Astatine is a rare chemical element, all of whose isotopes are unstable and decay.

clue.text: Knowledgeable, fine article penned by socialist

parts.note: well means in good health, fine

indicators.note: penned by means enclosed by the socialist's word

parts.note: red is a common label for a socialist
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A well-informed article written by a left-wing author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penned by' puts A inside RED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone well-read has absorbed much from books and is learned.

clue.text: It's possibly blooming nice prince?

parts.note: sweet means pleasant or nice
William is a British prince, heir to the throne

explanation.surface: A rhetorical question about whether a prince is pleasant, with blooming as a mild oath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blooming' reads as a British intensifier but means flowering.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet william is a garden plant with clusters of flowers, so an example of something in bloom.

clue.text: Upper floor of seats not right for kitchen area

indicators.note: not means the letter for right is left out

parts.note: a gallery is the raised tier of seats in a theatre

explanation.surface: A theatre's balcony is unsuitable as a place to cook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes R from GALLERY.
explanation.definitionFit: A galley is the cooking space on a ship or aircraft.

clue.text: Harry, angry about queen, heads off abroad, unhappy

indicators.note: about means the angry word surrounds the following letters

parts.note: mad means angry
R is from Regina, Latin for queen

indicators.note: heads off means taking the first letters of the following two words

explanation.surface: Prince Harry, furious about the Queen, heads overseas in a bad mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' places RAU inside MAD. 'Harry' looks like the prince but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To harry is to raid and harass, which is what marauders do.

clue.text: Everyone easily understood signal that danger is over

parts.note: all means everyone
clear means plain and easily understood

explanation.surface: Everybody grasps the sign that the threat has passed.
explanation.definitionFit: The all-clear is the siren after an air raid saying it is safe again.

clue.text: Insect about to bite one scoundrel

indicators.note: to bite means the about word closes its jaws round the next letters

parts.note: ca is short for circa, about
I is the Roman numeral one
a cad is a dishonourable man

explanation.surface: An insect is about to bite a rogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to bite' puts ICAD inside CA. 'about to' looks like 'going to'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cicada is a large insect known for its loud chirping song.

clue.text: Middle-distance runner caught sheep

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: An athlete chasing livestock catches a sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Steve Cram is a British athlete who held world records at 1500 metres and the mile.

clue.text: Practically perfect plan

indicators.note: practically means almost, so the word falls one letter short at the end

parts.note: ideal means perfect

explanation.surface: A scheme that is almost flawless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Practically' trims IDEAL to its first four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea can be a proposed scheme or intention, as in 'the idea is to leave early'.

clue.text: Grass, I recall, not half-cut

indicators.note: half-cut is British slang for drunk, so the letters reel into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone recalls they were not tipsy, or claims a lawn was not half mown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' looks like half a word removed, but it is slang for tipsy and shuffles I RECALL NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Citronella is a tropical grass whose oil is used in insect repellents.

clue.text: English knight draws empty conclusions

parts.note: N is the chess notation for knight

indicators.note: empty means the word is hollowed out, keeping only its outside letters

explanation.surface: An English knight reaches hollow verdicts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' keeps DS from draws.
explanation.definitionFit: Ends are finishes or conclusions.

clue.text: Having no post from me, duly open letters in a different order

indicators.note: in a different order means these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Without any mail from me, someone duly opens letters in a muddled order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'post' looks like mail but means a job.
explanation.definitionFit: Without a job or position you are out of work.
